transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. At work, at home... I feel like I’m a bad employee and a bad homeowner, like I deserve to lose what I’ve worked for.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a few weeks, or has this been going on for a couple of years?
It’s been going on for about two years and three months. It started after I bought my townhouse, when the pressure of keeping up with it started building.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a time like that, where I felt unusually energized or needed a lot less sleep.
Over these past two years, has there been any stretch of two months or longer where you felt essentially back to your normal self, without these feelings of guilt or low mood?

No, I don’t think there’s been a full two months where I felt like myself again. It’s been there almost the whole time—the low mood and not really being interested in things. There were brief times I could function a little better, but it didn’t last.

During these past two years, has there been a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood or lack of interest became noticeably worse than your usual baseline—more intense sadness, changes in sleep or appetite, or trouble concentrating that was clearly different from how you'd been feeling most of the time?

Looking back, I don’t think there was a separate two-week period where it got clearly worse than my usual. The low mood and not being interested in things have been there almost the whole time. I had brief times where I could function a little better, but they didn’t last.
